entry.name: VinT-6D
entry.title: VinT-6D: A Large-Scale Object-in-hand Dataset from Vision, Touch and Proprioception
entry.summary: Tencent's 3-finger TRX-Hand with a 620-taxel piezoresistive skin on fingers and palm holds one of 4 released objects while an ABB arm moves it through workspace poses; each snapshot pairs the activated-taxel positions with RGB-D, finger poses and Vicon object pose (plus a MuJoCo/Blender simulated split).
entry.hand: TRX-Hand (Tencent Robotics X, 3 fingers, 8 DoF) on an ABB arm; the simulated split uses a MuJoCo model of the same hand

sensor.note: Released touch is not per-taxel pressure. Each snapshot has touch_point_cloud.ply: x, y, z (float64, m) of the activated taxels in the hand frame, 5-53 points per real sample (median 11-31 per object). Paper: sensors respond above 250 Hz with a non-linear response to normal force; the released data are single snapshots about 1-2 s apart.
sensor.model: TRX-Hand whole-hand tactile skin (curved piezoresistive arrays)

scale.text: Released real split: 37,294 snapshots of 4 objects in 41 sessions (paper: 100,000 snapshots of 10 objects); simulated split: 57,500 TRX-Hand grasps of 23 objects x 16 rendered views (paper: 2M samples including an Allegro hand)

entry.access: Hugging Face vint6d/vint6d, ungated, MIT: real_trx_<object>.zip (4 files, 3.4 GB each) and syn_trx_<object>.zip (23 files, 1.5-3.4 GB); single samples can be read out of the zips with HTTP range requests.
caveats: Touch is released only as positions of activated taxels (touch_point_cloud.ply). No per-taxel pressure values, taxel IDs or taxel layout file are in the release.

Real data are snapshots, not continuous recordings: each object was grasped in about 10 sessions of roughly 950 snapshots taken 1-2 s apart while the arm moved through 125 positions x 8 hand rotations. The object stays in one grasp; there is no in-hand manipulation.
Only 4 of the paper's 10 real objects are released (folders 5, 7, 900, 904); names are not given in the release.
The simulated split contains only the TRX-Hand. No data from the 679-taxel Allegro skin described in the paper (simulated or real) is released.
No code, object meshes or marker-fixture models are in the release or linked from the project page (the paper says the fixtures are on the website; not found).
Simulated touch is a MuJoCo contact model (activated sensor positions), not measured data.

cameras.resolution: 640x565 depth (released: reprojected into the RGB camera, 640x400)

tracking.note: markers on a custom fixture per object; released as object2hand_pose.txt and object2camera_pose.txt (7 values each)
marker flange plate on the TRX-Hand; hand pose used for alignment, not released as its own file

other: object masks from SAM prompted with touch points
simulated split: MuJoCo grasps rendered in Blender with HDRI backgrounds, 16 views per grasp, train/val/test lists

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/vint6d/vint6d zip central directories of real_trx_05/07/900/904.zip and syn_trx_05.zip (range reads)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/vint6d/vint6d real_trx_05.zip sample_0304205435 (camera.json, rgb.png, depth.png, mask.png, touch_point_cloud.ply, 3 pose files) and syn_trx_05.zip sample_1716 (camera.json, scene_obj2cam.json, rgb/000000.jpg, depth/000000.png, test.txt)
unconfirmed: frames=37,294 counted from the real zips (rgb.png per sample folder: 9,286 / 9,463 / 8,999 / 9,546 for objects 5 / 7 / 900 / 904). It counts snapshots; the paper's 0.1M is for 10 objects.

Sessions: snapshot folder names are MMDDHHMMSS time stamps (year not encoded). Gaps over 60 s split them into 10 / 11 / 10 / 10 sessions of up to 964 snapshots, 1-2 s apart, recorded on 2024-03-03 to 03-12 (year assumed from the paper date). The paper describes 10 variations per object over 1,000 poses; the session-to-variation match is inferred.
Activated taxels per real snapshot (5-53, medians 31 / 19 / 27 / 11) derived from PLY file sizes (24 bytes per float64 vertex after a 144-145 byte header); one file opened to confirm (31 vertices).

Simulated split: 23 objects x 2,500 grasps = 57,500 grasps; each sample folder has 16 views (rgb/*.jpg, depth/*.png, mask/*.png). Counted in syn_trx_05.zip; the other 22 zips assumed to match. Simulated object ids (02-61, 901-903) follow YCB-Video numbering; real ids 5 and 7 would be YCB tomato soup can and tuna fish can, both named in the paper's tables, but the release does not say so.
Pose files hold 7 numbers: 3 translations (m, by range) + a unit quaternion; the quaternion order (wxyz or xyzw) is not documented.

Real depth.png is 16-bit with values 579-827 in the opened sample (mm by range; the real camera.json has no depth_scale, the simulated one has depth_scale 1.0). Only 19,089 of 256,000 pixels are non-zero in that sample, so the depth appears cropped to the hand-object region.
Tasks=1 (hold the grasped object while the arm moves); not a stated count. scenes=1: one robot platform.

zh.maker '腾讯Robotics X实验室' is from Chinese press coverage of the TRX-Hand (QbitAI, April 2023), not from the release, which is English only. The paper's first affiliation is Sun Yat-sen University; the TRX-Hand and data collection are Tencent Robotics X.
sensor.rate_hz null: the paper gives '>250 Hz' for the sensors, but released snapshots are 1-2 s apart.

zh.note: Paper, project page and dataset card are English only; the Chinese lab name comes from Chinese press coverage of the TRX-Hand.

sample.fetch_estimate: ~34 MB: 3 windows x 30 snapshots x ~0.37 MB (all files of each sample folder, sizes from the zip central directories), via range reads; ~45 MB of central directories already read. Re-hosted media: 30 RGB stills per episode, ~10 MB as PNG or far less as a re-encoded H.264 slideshow.
sample.rules_applied: 1 task (at most 6, so taken). With 3 tasks or fewer: 2-3 episodes per task and at least 3 in total, so 3 episodes from 3 different objects. The release has no continuous recordings: an episode is a window of 30 consecutive snapshots (1-2 s apart, 34-46 s) from one session, so the 10-60 s rule is met on the snapshot clock. Every real snapshot has at least 5 activated taxels (contact throughout). Simulated samples not sampled (simulated touch).
